title: The Beginning of a Proof
subtitle: A wise man once said, "A good start is half the battle." However, he forgot to mention what completes the rest of the battle.

items.text: The Beginning of a Proof

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The headquarters has issued a notice. The Critical Point of the "Storm" is in Vienna.
The chief assistant puts down Ms. Radio and turns around with a somber expression.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This type of Storm Syndrome involves a bodily transformation into oil paintings, primarily affecting the face but sometimes spreading to the torso. It is often accompanied by delirium and an intense obsession with war.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Like the "Storm" of 1929, it was accelerated by social upheavals resulting from the constant tensions Manus Vindictae created between nations.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This era ...
The color of the sky has changed.
The Storm Syndrome has finally reached this island.
No one on the team's caught it yet, but that could soon change.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: This is absurd!
With a bag filled with alchemy materials over her shoulders, the young pirate remains spirited despite a week in underground captivity.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: We went through all that trouble, sweated our guts out, and finally got to a place where the "Storm" can be kept out. But now you're telling me that immunity is going to disappear like a fart in the wind?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I was planning to stay here for a while. There might be alchemic materials and pieces of books the Abraxases left behind from their meals.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ugh! Now that is frustrating, mate!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: *sigh* Such is the nature of arcanum?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The immunity hasn't "disappeared." It's just waning. For now, only the beach has lost the effect. We're still safe around the Hall of Apeiron.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But there's no guarantee that we'll be safe here forever, right?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hah. Reminds me of Zeno's survival test.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto and I talked about this. We think the island is protected by a large-scale arcane ritual.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The sudden decay of the island's "Storm" immunity might be the result of its changes, though I'm unsure of the specifics.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Those people are doing something about it, right? That leader with the rock star hair—shouldn't he be taking action by now?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 6 has gathered all integers after the assembly. They're going to perform a mass cleansing ceremony.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 37 also mentioned a test. I think they have more than one way to deal with the changes.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: To the best of this APPLe's knowledge, secluded pure-blood arcanist groups often have rituals that they keep to themselves.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: These islanders impart Truth based on intellect and rationality, yet their doctrines are highly religious. Perhaps their arcane skills are passed down in a religious manner.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh, very mysterious, very arcane. I hope they're not all huddled together doing math at a time like this.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And I'm more worried about us, Captain.
Lilya changes her tone, unusually serious.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Arcana asked for more time for both sides to withdraw, didn't she?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. 6 gave us two hours to leave. That is to say ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We must set out when the "Storm" countdown reaches 20:00.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And before that, the stone bangle on your wrist still works, right?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. I can feel it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It would scald me whenever I thought about going to war with them.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hah. I see.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So we only have two hours for the plan.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Plan? What plan?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Aren't we sneaking away from all this?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Sorry, Regulus, your, uhm, "accommodation" was a long way from ours, so we haven't given you the latest updates.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: To put it simply ...

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Where are you going?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Uhm!
The sudden appearance of the girl startles the crowd.
37 stands there with a curious look on her face.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ahh, 37, we ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We are discussing how to leave this place, 37.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Precisely! I was just about to say, your chief wants us gone in a jiffy, but we don't even have a piece of wood to sail with!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Vertin is sizing us up to see if we can fit in her suitcase. She's going to swim across the Aegean Sea using her tiny arms! Right, Vertin?
Regulus squints and eagerly pokes her elbow in.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Right.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm. Sounds like a lot of fun!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Then you must leave from the north side of the beach, jump off the cliff there, and head south. The cliff is on the tangent line of the Hall of Apeiron, which is a good sign for your journey!
She nods confidently, fully convinced of her own conclusion.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I will show you where to jump. But you'll have to wait till Vertin and I return.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Me? Where are we going?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: What kind of question is that?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The only place worth going.
She extends her hand with a light and happy tone.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You're the one and only 0. We'll go see Apeiron together!
Guest Room, Island

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: Aren't you going to look for 37?

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: You took such good care of her while she was in a coma.
In the darkness, the figure trembles ever so slightly.
She tries to steady herself.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I don't know.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I don't know what I should do, Madam Marta.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: She's going back to the cave for the test, where I can't help her.
She looks down, trying her best to press her shaking hands together.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: All I can do is pray for her, for I have no adequate knowledge or power to assist her.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: As ever.

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: Perhaps you needn't worry so much.

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: 37 is the one favored by Truth. She will be fine.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I know. It's just ...
Sophia lets out a long, helpless sigh and buries her face deep in her palms.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: She is also of mortal flesh. She could get hurt, bleed, or die.
She avoids looking at the beach, seeing it as a battlefield where she lacks the skills to engage.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You haven't been with us for long, Madam Marta. Apeiron and Its test might be new to you.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Here on this island, we spent years theorizing, proving, and constructing models based on our mortal comprehension, defining the boundaries of what man is capable of understanding.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: But when it comes to the "essence" and "Forms," we are unable to make any definitive statements. So we humbly approach the temple and inquire about the correctness of our beliefs.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: And our answer is delivered as a "yes" or "no," reverberating in the form of echoes.

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: Is that the "submission of proof" 6 mentioned before?
The Corrector nods, knowing her friend has a natural talent for this.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Validating one's essence and soul with a number and verifying the authenticity of one's claims are simple feats for us.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: But Apeiron's test is different.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: "Those who succeed will obtain the transcendental Truth."

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: "Those who fail will pay a terrible price."

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Everything has its limits and boundaries.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Those who overstep their bounds will only court their own misfortune.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: We must respect and be wary of our limits, so our souls will be adequate for our bodies, and all things be refrained from excess.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: The "boundless," "limitless," and "infinity" are not of our realm to tread. They belong only to ancient beings that we cannot utter. We can only stand in awe, offering our admiration, humility, and reverence.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Now 37 is going to knock on Its door and ask to be indulged with the transcendental Truth. But, if she fails, if she can't bear the weight of the boundless infinity ...
She can't go on.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I wish I knew a better way, or could even do it in her place.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: But only she can do it. It has to be her, 37.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I'm sure this is the perfect solution to finally put an end to all our problems!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If I pass the test, Apeiron will grant me the answer to one question. It can be any question I don't have an answer to, even about the "essence" and "everything."

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: At least that's what Mama told me.
37 nods with confidence.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I just have to choose the right question to ask, and we will be rid of all the troubles. Whether it be the "Emanation," the turmoil of the phenomenal world, or the dangers threatening the island, all will be gone!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I have 6's blessing. He agrees with me. So, Vertin ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah-uh, not so fast! You can't just steal away our helmswoman like that!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: This "thing," it's too good to be without any risks, don't you think? What if Vertin doesn't make it back? Huh? Who's going to swim us across the sea then?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm? It could be risky, but not for Vertin, only for me. 0 multiplied by any number will still be 0.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: And we have validated that proof!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Well, that's not good enough for this Pirate! Besides, Vertin doesn't seem like a 0 to me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's okay, Regulus. I think I'll be safe there.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But 37, isn't this a sacred test for your people? I have never taken the oath. I'm not one of you.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: That does not matter, Vertin.
She gently shakes her head in determination.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But you must know that once we enter the temple, we cannot turn back. The path to the Truth is a one-way road.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Our last visit was interrupted, remember? You didn't get to ask your question, and I didn't get my answer.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: And now, I don't need to ask my question anymore.
She bites her lip, holding her own arms tight.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You and your friends were right, Vertin. The discord in the phenomenal world does have an effect on essence and Forms. No one can argue against this when facing the "Emanation."

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But there's more I'd like to know, and I believe you feel the same.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I will tell 6 that you're coming with me. I will tell everyone and persuade them, because this is the right thing to do.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Go, Timekeeper. While you're out, Lilya and I will ready us for evacuation.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: We will liaise with the Foundation from here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you both. I'm ready.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Before we go, 37, I have a question.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm?
A golden opportunity has arisen.
This could be a chance to level the playing field against Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You just said that Apeiron will grant an answer to whoever passes the test.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Will It answer my question?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If I asked for a way to become immune to the "Storm"?
TO BE CONTINUED…
